feed.title: Off the Roll: what's new
feed.subtitle: What has been added, by date: states, constituency and district pages, sources and tables on the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral rolls.

entry.title: 25 November 2026: 22 additions
entry.summary: A new page sets each state's draft roll of the 2027 summary revision against its final roll from the intensive revision, with the change, the electors by sex where reported, and the dates for claims and objections
entry.content:
• A new page sets each state's draft roll of the 2027 summary revision against its final roll from the intensive revision, with the change, the electors by sex where reported, and the dates for claims and objections
  • A new page lists the rules the revision's software reportedly used to flag logical discrepancies, each with the sources that report it, and lets a reader check which rules an entry like theirs would meet, without sending or storing anything
  • Uttar Pradesh: constituency figures counted from s1d labs' digitised rolls, against the 2022 margins, and the entries of the 2024 roll not found on the draft by age and sex, with women under 35 at 1.9 times the rate of men
  • West Bengal: a new page follows the appellate tribunals through every dated figure on appeals filed, decided and pending, with who gave each and where the sources differ
  • West Bengal: The Wire reported that the Commission's ECINet dashboard showed fixed figures for the state's electors with discrepancies and its notices, by an analysis of the system's code
  • Uttar Pradesh: 10,39,836 Form 6 applications in the first seven days of the summary revision, 3,99,218 of them on 22 November, the Chief Electoral Officer said, and Alt News counted repeat applications and electors deleted in the revision applying again
  • Jharkhand: the government moved a resolution in the Assembly on 25 November asking for the revision to be halted and a fresh procedure drawn up
  • West Bengal: the Supreme Court said it was inclined to stay the Calcutta High Court's order holding off the Kolkata municipal polls, and the Solicitor General is to take instructions by 30 November
  • The Supreme Court asked the Centre and the Government of Delhi to respond to the petitions over detentions during the October protests against the Chief Election Commissioner
  • West Bengal: tribunal judges were offered the option of working from home, The Telegraph reported, and an infant in Cooch Behar was refused a birth certificate after her father's name was deleted
  • Telangana: barely 1,000 of the 73.3 lakh electors left off the draft had filed fresh forms, and about 92 lakh of the 92.8 lakh notices were cleared by 20 November, The Times of India reported
  • Delhi: a delegation said the Chief Electoral Officer accepted that electors deleted as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate can be restored through an enumeration form, and the counts of forms to 23 November
  • Maharashtra: sex workers in Pune, Sangli and Jalgaon at risk of being left off the roll, The Times of India reported, and Jharkhand's Chief Electoral Officer found eligible young people missing in a sample check
  • Karnataka: a federation of parties and groups asked the State Election Commissioner to use the 2025 rolls for local elections
  • Events: Constitution Day gatherings on 26 November in Delhi, Nagpur, Patna, Jabalpur, Vijayawada, Kochi and eleven towns in Uttar Pradesh and Haryana
  • Further reading: Abhijnan Rej in The Interpreter on the software behind the rolls, and Kaleeswaram Raj in The New Indian Express on fighting political battles in court
  • Further reading: Diagram Chasing on Uttar Pradesh's rolls, which finds women under 35 left off the draft at twice the rate of men and counts errors on the final roll
  • A new page describes the datasets and analyses of the revision made by researchers, civic groups and newspapers, with how each was made, how it can be had and how its totals compare with the official figures
  • Further reading: new panels set the Samajwadi Party's duplicates claims, the Sabar Institute's count of seats and Human Rights Watch's figure of 130 million against the official numbers, and the Chief Minister's 1.27 crore claim now carries the Chief Electoral Officer's reply
  • Protests and disputes: choosing a state now shows where things stand there, with its roll figures, its summary revision, its next date in court and its latest items
  • Women: the page now sets women against men by age in Uttar Pradesh, women per 1,000 men at each stage of the revision in every state that publishes it, and the reports about women on the roll
  • Court cases: a new page follows each court matter on the revision, with its case numbers, every entry in date order and the next date listed

entry.title: 24 November 2026: 13 additions
entry.summary: West Bengal: the Supreme Court directed the appellate tribunals on 23 November to hear the appeals of deleted electors first and to defer appeals against inclusions for the time being
entry.content:
• West Bengal: the Supreme Court directed the appellate tribunals on 23 November to hear the appeals of deleted electors first and to defer appeals against inclusions for the time being
  • West Bengal: the Supreme Court issued notice on an application asking the state to withdraw notifications restricting deleted electors' access to welfare benefits, and said a person actually deprived may approach the High Court
  • Karnataka: the High Court declined on 20 November to stay the investigation into an FIR over Form 7 applications against the Jayanagar MLA and three others, and directed no arrest and no chargesheet without its leave, and listed the matter for 8 January 2027
  • Jharkhand: the Chief Electoral Officer said he expects the final roll of 22 December to hold around 2.33 crore electors, The Times of India reported
  • Andhra Pradesh: 769,000 enumeration forms handed out to electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, about 17.1% of them, Hindustan Times reported
  • Maharashtra: in Nagpur 1,18,099 electors left off the draft have been identified as enrolled elsewhere and the status of 13,25,412 is not established, The Hitavada reported
  • Delhi: the Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 23 November on forms disposed of and 32,95,950 electors issued notices parked for inclusion in the final roll
  • Delhi: no fresh Form 7 naming a BJP booth level agent as objector in Mustafabad since 5 November, The Hindu reported, and the Delhi Congress alleged that 75 living electors there were classified as dead
  • A report by Charchagram claims that personal data submitted through Form 6 was exposed on the Commission's portal for at least three years, The Hindu reported
  • Uttar Pradesh: the Samajwadi Party claimed around one lakh duplicate entries in the summary-revision draft and asked for the cash reward
  • Chhattisgarh: around 60,000 government school teachers will be away from class for nearly 81 days for SIR and Census duties, The New Indian Express reported
  • Further reading: Human Rights Watch's report on India, with its chapter on the revision, and the Reporters' Collective's response to Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer on its audit of 2024 polling-day records
  • Further reading: s1d labs' release of Uttar Pradesh's 2024, SIR and 2027 draft rolls as tables, read from the Commission's PDFs, with names and EPIC numbers replaced by tokens

entry.title: 23 November 2026: 9 additions
entry.summary: Uttar Pradesh: Alt News counted 1,10,875 electors on the summary-revision draft whose parent is listed with the same age or a younger one, in every district
entry.content:
• Uttar Pradesh: Alt News counted 1,10,875 electors on the summary-revision draft whose parent is listed with the same age or a younger one, in every district
  • Uttar Pradesh: the BJP began a three-day voter enrolment drive on 22 November, and its state president said Form 7 will be used if required against those he called 'ghuspaithiyas', PTI reported
  • Jharkhand: a community health centre wrote that a birth certificate questioned in Pakur was not issued through the civil registration portal, and the Chief Electoral Officer said no name is deleted without two notices, a hearing, physical verification and a reasoned order, The Times of India reported
  • Tamil Nadu: most of the 12.22 lakh Chennai electors classified as permanently shifted had yet to apply for inclusion, The Hindu reported
  • Punjab: a registration officer in Ludhiana directed that 33 teachers not be paid their November salaries over booth level officer duty, Hindustan Times reported
  • Events: gatherings in ten cities on Constitution Day, 26 November, a press conference in Mumbai on 24 November, a gathering at Jantar Mantar on 1 December, and a vigil at the Press Club of India on 22 November on transgender electors
  • Further reading: the reply of Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer's office to the Reporters' Collective's audit of 2024 polling-day records, and an explainer in The India Forum on whether the revision can be set right
  • Further reading: Joseph C. Mathew in The Hindu on the Commission's ECINet and ERONet and the powers the law gives registration officers, Niraja Gopal Jayal in The India Forum on voters and citizens, and Part 3 of the Reporters' Collective's audit of 2024 polling-day records, on Chittoor
  • Events: a discussion with Nitin Sethi, Vrinda Grover and Sravasti Dasgupta at the India Islamic Cultural Centre, New Delhi, on 28 November

entry.title: 22 November 2026: 11 additions
entry.summary: Form 7: unnamed officials told Deccan Chronicle that over 6 lakh names had been deleted in Telangana through Form 7 since 1 January, and that 79 lakh Form 7 applications came in this year, more than 13 times the count Telangana Today reported from the Chief Electoral Officer's office up to 31 Octobe
entry.content:
• Form 7: unnamed officials told Deccan Chronicle that over 6 lakh names had been deleted in Telangana through Form 7 since 1 January, and that 79 lakh Form 7 applications came in this year, more than 13 times the count Telangana Today reported from the Chief Electoral Officer's office up to 31 October
  • Telangana: 7,69,112 of the 19,41,444 electors left off Hyderabad district's draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate had been verified by 20 November, and officials had given out and collected only 10 forms, The New Indian Express reported
  • Notices: in Jharkhand 18,425 cases had been found ineligible for the final roll by 21 November, and 2,13,65,467 of 2,21,19,847 cases had been disposed of, The Times of India reported
  • Uttar Pradesh: the BJP is giving its booth level agents only Form 6 and Form 8 in the summary revision and no Form 7, party sources told The Indian Express
  • Form 7: in Indapur, Pune, over 6,300 objections were filed and 2,120 withdrawn, and at least 55 of the 100 sets of withdrawals were by BJP booth level agents, The Indian Express found
  • West Bengal: about 1 lakh appeals are pending from the 17 constituencies of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation as a tribunal judge resumed hearings, The Times of India reported
  • Courts: the Network of Women in Media, India, answered the Delhi Police's affidavit in the Supreme Court in a rejoinder of 21 November, Newslaundry and LiveLaw reported
  • Uttar Pradesh: Alt News found duplicate entries and other errors on the final roll in 69 polling stations it chose, and the Chief Electoral Officer answered a post on the electors left off with 'This is Revision not Treason'
  • Karnataka: the education department asked the Chief Electoral Officer on 17 November not to deploy teachers for the summary revision
  • RTI: Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer's office rejected an RTI query on the revision's publicity budget and spending, The Hindu reported
  • Events: a BJP Maha Padayatra in Karimnagar on 23 November led by Nitin Nabin, and a Mahila Congress protest in Thiruvananthapuram on 21 November

entry.title: 21 November 2026: 11 additions
entry.summary: West Bengal: the office of the Chief Electoral Officer postponed the special summary revision due to begin with the draft roll on 23 November, by a press note of 20 November that gives no new dates, and its campaign days are no longer listed
entry.content:
• West Bengal: the office of the Chief Electoral Officer postponed the special summary revision due to begin with the draft roll on 23 November, by a press note of 20 November that gives no new dates, and its campaign days are no longer listed
  • Maharashtra: the Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 20 November sets out how electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate can return through regenerated enumeration forms until 30 November, with special camps on 28 and 29 November
  • Special campaign days: Punjab holds one on 22 November at every polling booth, by the Chief Electoral Officer's post on X
  • Form 7: in Bhusawal, Maharashtra, only 74 electors were found eligible for deletion out of 14,567 Form 7 objections received by post, and the registration officer disposed of all of them on 17 November, The Indian Express reported
  • Form 7: 5,585 Form 7 objections were digitised in Jharkhand on 19 November, taking the total to 1,75,398, The Times of India reported
  • West Bengal: the Commission changed the appellate tribunals' portal as the judges asked, and the tribunals have begun uploading their orders again after a gap of nearly 45 days, sources told The Times of India
  • Uttar Pradesh: the Independent Commission on the SIR, chaired by Justice Madan B. Lokur, asked the Chief Minister on 21 November for the material behind his reported statement on electors excluded from the roll, LiveLaw reported
  • Courts: Newslaundry set the accounts of journalists detained during the October protests against the Delhi Police's affidavit in the Supreme Court
  • Further reading: The Wire on transgender electors on the rolls of 12 states and union territories, and, on 2024 polling-day records, the Reporters' Collective's report on votes after 5 pm and the reply the Chief Electoral Officers of Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir posted
  • Further reading: the Sabar Institute's preliminary report on the names left off Uttar Pradesh's draft roll, with a page for each of the state's 403 constituencies, which finds that 22.0% of women and 16.5% of men on the 2022 roll were left off
  • Draft rolls: Punjab's summary-revision draft of 12 November stayed equal to the final roll of the special revision, 2.01 crore, because the applications received had not yet been processed, Punjabi Jagran reported from what the Chief Electoral Officer, Anindita Mitra, said

entry.title: Week ending 20 November 2026
entry.summary: The Commission's letter of 17 November sets 18 to 30 November for handing out and collecting the enumeration forms of electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate in seven states and 10 December for deciding them, and moves the final rolls of Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh
entry.content:
• How the revision was run. The Commission's letter of 17 November sets 18 to 30 November for handing out and collecting the enumeration forms of electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate in seven states and 10 December for deciding them, and moves the final rolls of Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland from 30 November to 22 December, as Hindustan Times reported.
  • How the revision was run. The Commission ordered summary revisions in Karnataka and Meghalaya on 16 November, with draft rolls on 1 December, claims and objections until 31 December and final rolls on 20 January 2027.
  • Protests and disputes. The Supreme Court said on 17 November that the batch on the Commission's functioning will be heard on 9 December, and on 19 November it closed the Mustafabad Form 7 petition and posted the Delhi petition of Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri to 2 December, asking the Commission's counsel how many enumeration forms had been filled and how many Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 applications had been made.
  • How the revision was run. Uttar Pradesh's summary-revision draft of 17 November has 13,58,68,905 electors, 18,84,113 more than the final roll of 10 April, and the drafts of Goa, Uttarakhand, Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have 10,89,381, 72,78,035, 57,701 and 2,60,981.
  • Protests and disputes. In Jharkhand 41,03,251 of 45,49,961 logical discrepancy cases and 10,42,976 of 14,03,981 no-mapping cases had been disposed of by 19 November, Amar Ujala reported.
  • Protests and disputes. Deccan Chronicle reported on 19 November that only nine enumeration forms had come in from the 73,39,234 Telangana electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and The Reporters' Collective reported that the office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer had told the Commission that printing and sorting the forms would take at least a month.
  • Protests and disputes. The Hindu found that at least 1,13,059 new enrolments on Bengaluru's final rolls could not be traced to Form 6 or Form 8 records, and that at least 1,635 people listed for deletion across the city are in the final roll with the same EPIC numbers.
  • For journalists. A page for journalists now says how to cite each page, reuse the charts and tables under their licence, find the source behind a figure and use the words for names left off and deleted, and a guide works through Tamil Nadu's figures from its pages and downloads to what the data cannot show.

entry.title: 20 November 2026: 13 additions
entry.summary: What's new: the week ending 20 November in 8 sentences, each linked to the page that carries the fact, at the top of this page. A new issue follows every Friday
entry.content:
• What's new: the week ending 20 November in 8 sentences, each linked to the page that carries the fact, at the top of this page. A new issue follows every Friday
  • Courts: the Supreme Court heard the Delhi petition of Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri on 19 November, posted it to 2 December and asked the Commission's counsel how many enumeration forms had been filled and how many Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 applications had been made, Hindustan Times reported
  • Court calendar: the Delhi petition is listed again on 2 December, when the bench is to take stock of the figures the Commission files
  • Delhi: Delhi's Deputy Chief Electoral Officer asked the Commission how to carry out its order on fresh enumeration forms for electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and the office said printing and sorting the forms would take at least a month, The Reporters' Collective reported
  • Delhi: the Chief Electoral Officer's bulletin of 19 November gives 3,18,409 Form 6 applications and 33,018 Form 7 objections received since the draft of 31 August, and the Ministry of Home Affairs transferred the Chief Electoral Officer, Ashok Kumar, to Jammu and Kashmir on 18 November, The Indian Express reported
  • Telangana: only nine enumeration forms had come in from the 73,39,234 electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, Deccan Chronicle reported on 19 November, and ETV Bharat reported that 15 had been reinstated in Hyderabad district
  • Karnataka: The Hindu found that at least 1,635 people listed for deletion across Bengaluru are in the final roll with the same EPIC numbers, and that in at least 290 cases the EPIC numbers of people marked for deletion had been transferred or reissued to different people, by the parts of its reports the paper shows free
  • Notices: in Jharkhand 41,03,251 of 45,49,961 logical discrepancy cases and 10,42,976 of 14,03,981 no-mapping cases had been disposed of by 19 November, Amar Ujala reported
  • West Bengal: housekeeping staff of the appellate tribunals at Joka went on strike on 19 November after being paid for one of the four months they had worked, The Times of India reported
  • Andhra Pradesh: the Chief Electoral Officer's press release of 19 November sets out how electors left off the draft of 31 July as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate can return through regenerated enumeration forms until 30 November, keeping their EPIC numbers, before the final roll on 22 December
  • Special campaign days: Bihar's are 21 and 22 November and 5 and 6 December at every polling station, by the Chief Electoral Officer's direction that Live Hindustan reported
  • Events: a Congress Samvidhan Raksha March in Bhopal on 26 November, a people's convention in Hyderabad on 22 November and an INDIA bloc rally proposed for Bhopal on 12 December
  • Further reading: Reuters on the US Commission on International Religious Freedom's statement on the revisions, and Deccan Herald's editorial on the summary revision as a chance to undo the special revision's wrongs

entry.title: 19 November 2026: 13 additions
entry.summary: Draft rolls: the Andaman and Nicobar Islands' summary-revision draft of 17 November has 2,60,981 electors, 1,31,829 men, 1,29,149 women and 3 third gender, which is 2,941 more than its final roll, by the Chief Electoral Officer's figures
entry.content:
• Draft rolls: the Andaman and Nicobar Islands' summary-revision draft of 17 November has 2,60,981 electors, 1,31,829 men, 1,29,149 women and 3 third gender, which is 2,941 more than its final roll, by the Chief Electoral Officer's figures
  • Courts: the Supreme Court on 19 November closed the Mustafabad Form 7 petition, directing the Election Commission and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer to verify the petitioner's information and take remedial measures, without expressing an opinion on the allegations
  • Courts: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri asked the Supreme Court in the Delhi case to extend Delhi's timeline, to see the Commission's letter of 6 November carried out, and to order an audit of Form 7 applications, LiveLaw reported
  • Courts: Karnataka and its State Election Commission asked the Supreme Court to let Bengaluru's corporation elections go ahead on the ward rolls of April 2026, saying the city's electorate fell from about 1.03 crore to 59.08 lakh after the revision, The Indian Express reported
  • Courts: the Supreme Court sought replies on 18 November to a plea by Delhi traders over business losses during the October protests against the Chief Election Commissioner, with a hearing set tentatively for 27 November
  • Uttar Pradesh: Pilibhit's Chief Judicial Magistrate on 18 November sought reports on an application against the district's former District Election Officer and others, with 2 December as the next date
  • Uttar Pradesh: overseas electors rose from 3,625 on the final roll to 4,215 on the summary-revision draft, and the Chief Electoral Officer asked those enrolled as ordinary electors to surrender their cards and apply on Form 6A, The Times of India reported. The draft rolls are now searchable PDFs
  • Uttarakhand: booth level officers check their rolls for names entered twice from 20 to 27 November, and duplicates are to be deleted through Form 7, Live Hindustan reported
  • Notices: more than 32.8 lakh of over 33 lakh notices in Delhi had been addressed, NDTV reported on 18 November from the Commission's figures
  • Telangana and Delhi: Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer set 18 to 30 November for the forms of electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and Delhi's booth level officers were still awaiting the forms on 18 November, PTI reported
  • Further reading: The Wire on what a notice costs electors in Jharkhand, and The Federal on West Bengal's pending appeals before the summary revision
  • For journalists: how to cite these pages, reuse the charts and tables under their licence, find the source behind a figure and use the words for names left off and deleted, with the feeds, calendars and downloads in one place
  • What to do now: the WhatsApp button on each state's page now sends every step and date in the page's summary, in the page's language, and a second button copies the same message for any other app

entry.title: 18 November 2026: 12 additions
entry.summary: Seven states: the Commission's letter of 17 November sets 18 to 30 November for handing out and collecting the enumeration forms of electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and 10 December for deciding them, and moves the final rolls of Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh,
entry.content:
• Seven states: the Commission's letter of 17 November sets 18 to 30 November for handing out and collecting the enumeration forms of electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, and 10 December for deciding them, and moves the final rolls of Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland from 30 November to 22 December, as Hindustan Times reported
  • Delhi: the Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 17 November sets out the drive for electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, with the same EPIC number re-assigned once a form is accepted
  • Form 7: the Karnataka High Court on 17 November stayed further investigation in three more FIRs against BJP booth level agents over Form 7 applications, in Mysuru, Jayanagar and Kodagu, and deferred the State's applications to vacate the earlier stays in Malleshwaram
  • Courts: Delhi Police told the Supreme Court that its direction of 11 October protecting journalists at the October protests does not cover reel-makers and social media influencers, and that complaints by women journalists against police officers had been closed, Bar and Bench and LiveLaw reported
  • Courts: Delhi Police asked a magistrate's court on 17 November for more time on an application for an FIR against the Chief Election Commissioner, saying heavy law and order duty had kept it from an enquiry, The New Indian Express reported
  • Courts: the Delhi case on the Form 6 declaration is item 26 before the Chief Justice's bench on 19 November, with W.P.(C) No. 1339 of 2026 connected to it, by the Supreme Court's cause list
  • Uttar Pradesh: the Chief Electoral Officer set the summary-revision draft of 13.58 crore against a projected 16.16 crore adults, and 11.83 lakh electors aged 18 or 19 against a projected 84.47 lakh, Live Hindustan reported, and said the roll's database holds no details of religion or caste
  • Uttar Pradesh: booth level officers now get an alert when an applicant is already registered or has another application pending, The Times of India reported
  • Andaman and Nicobar Islands: the CPI(M) walked out of the Chief Electoral Officer's meeting with parties on 17 November when its demand that electors left off in the revision be put back on the roll first was refused
  • Maharashtra: Nagpur district had received 65,829 Form 6 applications by 13 November, 38,533 online and 27,296 on paper, The Times of India reported
  • Events: a Congress Constitution march in Panchkula and a BJP rally in Kolkata, both on 26 November, and a BJP padayatra in Diglipur on 17 November. The Congress's Delhi Chalo marches of 25 and 26 November were postponed, The Times of India reported, and are no longer listed
  • Further reading: Deccan Herald sets the summary-revision drafts of 13 states and union territories against their final rolls

entry.title: 17 November 2026: 10 additions
entry.summary: Courts: the Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant said on 17 November that the batch on the Commission's functioning will be heard on 9 December, after the Election Commission files its objections to the INDIA bloc leaders' application to serve 48 interrogatories, Bar and Bench reported
entry.content:
• Courts: the Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant said on 17 November that the batch on the Commission's functioning will be heard on 9 December, after the Election Commission files its objections to the INDIA bloc leaders' application to serve 48 interrogatories, Bar and Bench reported
  • Courts: Ali Mehdi, the Congress candidate for Mustafabad in 2025, asked the Supreme Court on 16 November to act on what The Hindu calls ghost Form 7s in Mustafabad, which the summary of the report says listed living electors as dead and electors found at home as shifted
  • West Bengal: electors whose eligibility is still under adjudication before judicial officers have not reached the appellate tribunals, and unnamed sources put them at over 25,000 in Murshidabad, Malda, Nadia and Howrah, The Indian Express reported
  • Draft rolls: Uttar Pradesh's summary-revision draft of 17 November has 13,58,68,905 electors, 18,84,113 more than the final roll of 10 April, and Goa's draft of 12 November has 10,89,381, which is 31,815 more than its final roll
  • Karnataka and Meghalaya: the Commission ordered a summary revision on 16 November, with draft rolls on 1 December, claims and objections until 31 December and final rolls on 20 January 2027, as Hindustan Times and The Hindu reported
  • Uttar Pradesh: the Congress applied to a Pilibhit court on 16 November for an FIR against the District Election Officer over the roll of Pilibhit Sadar, Hindustan Times reported
  • Uttar Pradesh: 38 of 42 teachers at one Ghaziabad inter college and 34 of 36 at another were away on booth level officer duty for the summary revision on 16 November, The Times of India reported
  • Karnataka: The Hindu found that at least 1,13,059 new enrolments on Bengaluru's final rolls could not be traced to Form 6 or Form 8 records, 44% of the new enrolments, by the summary the paper shows free
  • Delhi: 31,027 Form 6 applications came in between 29 October and 15 November, about 3.10 lakh since the draft, and officials said the schedule may be extended again, PTI reported
  • Events: a Congress 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' chaupal in Tauru, Haryana, on 16 November

entry.title: 16 November 2026: 8 additions
entry.summary: Courts: INDIA bloc leaders asked the Supreme Court on 16 November for leave to put 48 written questions to the Election Commission, to be answered on affidavit by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu, the Chief Election Commissioner, the two Election Commissioners and the Director Gener
entry.content:
• Courts: INDIA bloc leaders asked the Supreme Court on 16 November for leave to put 48 written questions to the Election Commission, to be answered on affidavit by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu, the Chief Election Commissioner, the two Election Commissioners and the Director General (IT), on how the Commission approved its affidavits and orders, the Election Commissioners' recorded dissents, the West Bengal appeals, access to ECINET and approvals given by WhatsApp, Business Standard reported
  • Courts: Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders told the Supreme Court in a rejoinder that the Election Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October came with no minutes, file notings or recorded approvals to show that all three Commissioners approved the revision, The Wire reported
  • Courts: the batch of petitions on the Commission's functioning is item 26 before the Chief Justice's bench on 17 November, with the INDIA bloc leaders' petition as item 26.5, by the Supreme Court's cause list, and Bar and Bench names the eleven leaders who sought leave to serve the interrogatories
  • Karnataka: the Chief Minister announced on 15 November that the police would collect household records door to door across Bengaluru, saying the city's roll had shrunk from 51 lakh to 45 lakh, The Indian Express reported
  • Form 7: ten days after the Commission's letter of 6 November, enumeration forms had not been generated for the 20.60 million electors left off Maharashtra's draft roll, and officials told Hindustan Times on 16 November that the final roll due on 30 November is likely to be delayed
  • Notices: in Telangana 54,863 electors had been found ineligible after a notice and hearings were completed for 92,78,967, as of 14 November, Telangana Today reported
  • Further reading: Reuters on families whose relatives were detained, deported or questioned about their citizenship after their names were dropped from the rolls, and Hindustan Times on about 50 lakh electors added in nine states' summary-revision drafts
  • Looking closer at a state's figures: a guide that works through Tamil Nadu, from its pages and downloads to how each figure is worked out, which datasets can be set beside the roll, the thresholds the data are held to, what the data cannot show, and how the public hearings on the revision were run

entry.title: 15 November 2026: 6 additions
entry.summary: Courts: the Election Commission told the Supreme Court in a supplementary affidavit of 14 November that electors left off the draft roll in the revising states may submit the enumeration form, that booth-wise lists of electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate are to be displayed afresh, and
entry.content:
• Courts: the Election Commission told the Supreme Court in a supplementary affidavit of 14 November that electors left off the draft roll in the revising states may submit the enumeration form, that booth-wise lists of electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate are to be displayed afresh, and that electors who have already filed Form 6 need not file again, The Hindu, The Indian Express and PTI reported
  • Form 7: in Pune, 57 of 58 Bhosari electors named in a complaint were among 5,603 for whom the software generated a Form 7 after address changes were accepted in other constituencies, The Indian Express found, and the Pimpri assistant registration officer filed a police report on 1 November over 40 Form 8 applications filed from four mobile numbers
  • Uttar Pradesh: booth level officers found responsible for errors in the roll between 17 November and 16 December may lose up to a month's honorarium, by the Chief Electoral Officer's direction of 14 November that The Times of India reported
  • West Bengal: Jawhar Sircar, a former Chief Electoral Officer of the state, asked its Chief Electoral Officer on 13 November who ordered the appeals against 16,10,311 electors whom judicial officers had found eligible, The Wire reported
  • Draft rolls: Madhya Pradesh's draft of 12 November holds 2,82,85,144 men, 2,65,13,547 women and 937 third gender electors, by PTI's report
  • Events: the Congress has asked its units to hold village chaupals until 15 December at which deleted names are to be read out, and marches on Constitution Day, 26 November, among them a yatra by its Uttar Pradesh unit

entry.title: 14 November 2026: 6 additions
entry.summary: Draft rolls: Lakshadweep's summary-revision draft of 12 November has 57,701 electors, by the Chief Electoral Officer's press note, and Uttarakhand's has 72,78,035, as the Additional Chief Electoral Officer gave the figures to Dainik Jagran and Aaj Tak
entry.content:
• Draft rolls: Lakshadweep's summary-revision draft of 12 November has 57,701 electors, by the Chief Electoral Officer's press note, and Uttarakhand's has 72,78,035, as the Additional Chief Electoral Officer gave the figures to Dainik Jagran and Aaj Tak
  • Special campaign days: Uttar Pradesh's are 21, 22, 28 and 29 November at every polling station, by the Chief Electoral Officer's note of 13 November, and West Bengal's are 28 and 29 November and 5, 6, 12, 13, 19 and 20 December, by its Chief Electoral Officer's press note of the same day
  • Form 7: Maharashtra received 23,60,021 online applications for inclusion, deletion and correction from the draft of 31 August to 12 November, The Times of India reported
  • Notices: of the 1.22 crore electors served notices in Maharashtra, 72,601 had not cleared because their documents were not yet submitted or still being checked, Hindustan Times reported on 14 November
  • West Bengal: The Wire counted 29,347 electors still under adjudication in 304 polling stations of 11 Murshidabad constituencies, against the 815 undecided cases the Chief Electoral Officer's office gave the Calcutta High Court's Registrar General

entry.title: Week ending 13 November 2026

entry.content:
• How the revision was run. The Commission wrote on 6 November to the Chief Electoral Officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland that electors left off the draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate can be included in the final roll by submitting the enumeration form with a statement, and that a form accepted keeps the elector's earlier EPIC number.
  • How the revision was run. The summary-revision draft rolls of Uttar Pradesh and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are now due on 17 November, with claims and objections until 16 December and the final rolls on 4 January 2027, and Gujarat's draft is due on 27 November with the final roll on 18 January 2027.
  • Protests and disputes. Karnataka's State Election Commission asked the Supreme Court on 12 November to let it hold the five Bengaluru corporation elections on the final rolls of 18 April 2026 and to complete them by 31 January 2027.
  • Protests and disputes. The Calcutta High Court issued notice on 12 November on a petition over an Economically Weaker Section certificate withheld because a parent was deleted from the roll, and LiveLaw reported on 13 November that the court had agreed to hear an Army aspirant refused a domicile certificate because his mother was deleted.
  • Protests and disputes. The Wire found that 14,39,797 of the 16,08,175 West Bengal electors whom judicial officers found eligible and the Commission has appealed against have Muslim names by its classification, and the Hindustan Times reported from a report by the Civic Research Group that in 7,335 polling booths across 23 districts every elector found eligible faces an appeal against inclusion.
  • How the revision was run. Assam's summary-revision draft roll, published on 12 November, has 2,51,76,910 electors, 2,18,771 more than the final roll of the special revision of 10 February, as Pratidin Time reported the Chief Electoral Officer's figures.
  • How the revision was run. In Delhi 32,35,212 of the electors sent the 33.1 lakh notices had been parked for the final roll by 4 November, and Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer put the electors found ineligible after a notice at 54,418 on 6 November.
  • Kerala 2026. Each state overview with both counts draws the names left off the draft as squares with the names added after the draft filled in over them, and every Kerala constituency page and every Kerala and Karnataka district page shows where the place sits among all the state's constituencies or districts on each measure.

entry.title: 13 November 2026: 17 additions
entry.summary: What's new: the week ending 13 November in 8 sentences, each linked to the page that carries the fact, at the top of this page. A new issue follows every Friday
entry.content:
• What's new: the week ending 13 November in 8 sentences, each linked to the page that carries the fact, at the top of this page. A new issue follows every Friday
  • Courts: Karnataka's State Election Commission asked the Supreme Court on 12 November to let it hold the elections to the five city corporations of the Greater Bengaluru Authority on the final rolls of 18 April 2026 and to complete them by 31 January 2027 in place of 31 December 2026, saying the Election Commission had not supplied complete roll data since the final roll of 27 October, Deccan Herald reported
  • Courts: the Calcutta High Court agreed to hear an Army aspirant refused a domicile certificate because his mother was deleted from the roll in the revision, LiveLaw reported on 13 November
  • Courts: the family of six whom the Bombay High Court at Goa ordered on 5 November to be included in the roll of Santa Cruz are in the draft roll published on 12 November, Goa's Chief Electoral Officer said, and one of them has filed a caveat in the Supreme Court, The Times of India reported
  • Form 7: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer counted 5,16,752 Form 6 and 82,425 Form 7 applications since the revision began, 3,04,352 and 30,954 of them after the draft roll of 31 August, by a bulletin to 11 November that the Hindustan Times reported. Claims close on 25 November, and forms for electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate are to be handed out from next week
  • Events: People Against SIR has called for peaceful protests across the country from 26 November to 20 December, beginning with demonstrations on Constitution Day, The Hindu reported on 12 November
  • Further reading: Priya Seetharaman's column in The Hindu of 13 November, which reads the revision as a digital project run on the Commission's ERONet platform and describes the rules coded into it that decided who received a notice and who had to appear for a hearing
  • Draft rolls: a table of the summary revision's draft rolls in all 23 states and union territories it covers, with the count of electors on each draft found so far, the change from the final roll of the intensive revision, the source and a note on each figure
  • Draft rolls: each state's overview and its "What to do now" page give the count of electors on its summary-revision draft beside the final roll of the intensive revision, or say that the draft was due and no count has been found
  • Assam: the draft roll of the summary revision, published on 12 November, has 2,51,76,910 electors, 2,18,771 more than the final roll of the special revision of 10 February, as Pratidin Time reported the Chief Electoral Officer's figures
  • Kerala and Karnataka: every Kerala constituency page and every Kerala and Karnataka district page now shows where the place sits among all the state's constituencies or districts on each measure, with the median marked, and sets each of its rolls against the median place's
  • Andaman and Nicobar Islands: the Chief Electoral Officer's release of 12 November says the Commission moved the union territory's summary-revision draft to 17 November, with claims and objections until 16 December and the final roll still due on 4 January
  • Special campaign days: the days on which booth level officers sit at the polling stations to take claims, for six states and union territories and three districts so far, are in the table of draft rolls and on each state's "What to do now" page
  • Further reading: Aman Bhargava's analysis for Diagram Chasing of Karnataka's final roll, read by machine and joined to the earlier rolls, which finds about 14,900 of 1,05,48,148 electors left off the draft back on the final roll in the same constituency, and 3,115 told they were not on the 2002 roll who are on it
  • Every state overview with both counts now draws the names left off the draft as squares, with the names added after the draft filled in over them
  • The constituency and district tables on 13 state pages shade each rate column from its lowest figure to its highest, so the highest stand out without sorting
  • Gujarat: the summary-revision draft is due on 27 November, with claims until 26 December and the final roll on 18 January 2027, as Divya Bhaskar, Gujarati Jagran and Gujarat Vandan reported a press note of the Chief Electoral Officer of 29 October

entry.title: 12 November 2026: 7 additions
entry.summary: Courts: in 7,335 polling booths across 23 districts of West Bengal, every elector whom judicial officers found eligible faces an appeal against inclusion before the appellate tribunals, the Hindustan Times reported on 11 November from a report by the Civic Research Group. entry.content:
• Courts: in 7,335 polling booths across 23 districts of West Bengal, every elector whom judicial officers found eligible faces an appeal against inclusion before the appellate tribunals, the Hindustan Times reported on 11 November from a report by the Civic Research Group. The paper reports that appeals against 21,615 of the 27,277 such electors in those booths were pending. The group's own count is 16,08,175 appeals against inclusion in the state, 15,26,933 of them pending
  • Courts: the Calcutta High Court issued notice on 12 November on a petition over an Economically Weaker Section certificate withheld from a son because his parent was deleted from the roll in the revision, and asked the West Bengal government for a report on a student refused a passport because his mother was deleted
  • Form 7: the electoral registration officer for Bhiwandi East in Maharashtra told the Hindustan Times on 12 November that his office had received 540 Form 7 applications and rejected over 450, because the electors were found living at their addresses, after the Chief Electoral Officer told registration officers to put the burden of proof on objectors
  • Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh named the Moradabad Divisional Commissioner, on the Commission's direction, to hold an inquiry against the two suspended Pilibhit SDMs, Amar Ujala reported on 12 November
  • Protests and disputes: Karnataka's State Election Commission told the five Bengaluru corporations on 5 November to prepare their ward rolls from the final Assembly rolls of 27 October, Deccan Herald reported
  • Protests and disputes: the Biju Janata Dal alleged on 11 November that residents of Kotia and Jumdang on Odisha's border with Andhra Pradesh hold voter cards from both states after Odisha's revision, and the Koraput Collector said about 10% of Kotia's voters voted in Andhra Pradesh's panchayat elections
  • Further reading and viewing: three Frontline videos, Ayesha Minhaz's documentary on the revision in Telangana and interviews with Prashant Bhushan and Prasenjit Bose

entry.title: 11 November 2026: 7 additions
entry.summary: Form 7: The Hindu reported on 10 November that the 796 Form 7 applications naming 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP as objectors in Delhi's Mustafabad are mostly in 25 of its 294 booths, are all against Muslim electors by the paper's account, and are over 76% of the 1,044 deletion applicati
entry.content:
• Form 7: The Hindu reported on 10 November that the 796 Form 7 applications naming 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP as objectors in Delhi's Mustafabad are mostly in 25 of its 294 booths, are all against Muslim electors by the paper's account, and are over 76% of the 1,044 deletion applications in the constituency. It found at least 87 of the electors named living at their registered addresses. The Delhi BJP said its agents filed no Form 7s there
  • Form 7: The Hindu reported on 15 October that the Commission's software generated Form 7s in registration officers' names when officials deleted electors at hearings in Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal, and that no written procedure for these forms was shared with the states
  • Courts: a Sessions Judge refused on 30 October to stay a Haldwani magistrate's order to register an FIR over Form 7s filed to delete 28 electors, and the police's revision petition is listed for 7 December
  • Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's panchayat and urban local body rolls hold 16.90 crore electors against 13.52 crore on the Assembly rolls, 3.38 crore apart, Live Hindustan reported on 11 November. In Makdoompur village in Rae Bareli an inquiry ordered by the High Court examined 448 electors on the panchayat roll and off the Assembly roll, and 114 eligible electors were added
  • Courts: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, petitioners in the Supreme Court on Delhi's revision, wrote to the Commission on 10 November asking that the remedies of its letter of 6 November to seven states be given to every elector left off a draft roll as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate
  • Events: the Independent Young Citizens Collective will hold a rally on Anna Salai in Chennai on 26 November
  • Further reading and viewing: Manish Tewari in The Tribune on internal migration and the names left off the drafts, and The Wire on names left off in booths the Congress won strongly in Karnataka

entry.title: 10 November 2026: 10 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath, said on 8 November that about 1.27 crore Hindu voters on the rolls of the state's panchayat elections are missing from the Election Commission's rolls after the revision, The Indian Express reported. The Samajwadi Party presiden
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath, said on 8 November that about 1.27 crore Hindu voters on the rolls of the state's panchayat elections are missing from the Election Commission's rolls after the revision, The Indian Express reported. The Samajwadi Party president, Akhilesh Yadav, asked how he had figures by religion when the Commission had released none
  • Protests and disputes: a delegation of opposition parties and civil society groups met Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer on 9 November on the Commission's letter of 6 November. By the delegation's account, he accepted that electors left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate can be restored by an enumeration form with their earlier EPIC numbers, and a standard operating procedure is to follow
  • How the revision ran: the Commission approved a revised summary-revision programme for Uttar Pradesh, which the Chief Electoral Officer announced on 10 November. The draft roll is now to be published on 17 November, claims and objections taken until 16 December and decided by 28 December, and the final roll published on 4 January 2027
  • Further reading and viewing: the panel on Yogi Adityanath now carries his interview with Aaj Tak of 8 November on 1.27 crore Hindu voters he says are on the panchayat rolls and missing from the Commission's rolls, set beside Uttar Pradesh's roll before the revision and its final roll
  • Protests and disputes: The Reporters' Collective reported on 7 November that 1,82,440 electors whom the Commission marked dead and left off Rajasthan's draft roll are on the State Election Commission's panchayat roll as living electors
  • Form 7: Gadarpur's registration officer and ten assistant registration officers filed 2,742 objections on 18 and 28 September, after claims and objections had closed on 13 August, by the Chief Electoral Officer's own records as Newslaundry reported them. In Andhra Pradesh, The News Minute found officers named as objectors for 20,959 electors in the last 12 days of claims, and the Chief Electoral Officer replied that the forms are generated in the officer's name after a speaking order
  • Protests and disputes: the retired judge Biswajit Basu resigned on 7 November from one of West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals, and the Allahabad High Court held on 2 November that government teachers can be given booth level officer duty
  • Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's roll held 1.21 crore fewer women than men on 7 October, and the Chief Electoral Officer ordered a drive to enrol women. Ghaziabad is to use the Census 2027 enumeration to find adults missing from the roll, and the state now has 3,786 fewer polling stations
  • Protests and disputes: West Bengal's opposition parties asked for Form 6 re-entry for the 27 lakh electors deleted by judicial officers, Hyderabad's District Election Officer said no illegal immigrant was found on the district's rolls, a Hazaribag official was suspended over a bribe for SIR corrections, and Karnataka's ministers and a Muslim body raised the state's names left off
  • Further reading and viewing: Frontline on Karnataka's electorate after the revision, Anjali Bhardwaj, Amrita Johri and Yogendra Yadav on the Commission's letter of 6 November, Venkatesh Nayak on the Commission's refusals under the RTI Act, and The Hindu's editorial on the rolls and welfare

entry.title: 9 November 2026: 3 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: The Wire's analysis of appeal records compiled by the Civic Research Group finds that 14,39,797 of the 16,08,175 West Bengal electors whom judicial officers found eligible and the Election Commission has appealed against, 89.5 per cent, have Muslim names by its classification.
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: The Wire's analysis of appeal records compiled by the Civic Research Group finds that 14,39,797 of the 16,08,175 West Bengal electors whom judicial officers found eligible and the Election Commission has appealed against, 89.5 per cent, have Muslim names by its classification. Muslims are 27 per cent of the state's population by the 2011 census
  • Protests and disputes: a petition before the Kolhapur bench of the Bombay High Court asks for every elector deleted in Maharashtra in the revision to be restored and for fourteen orders of the Commission to be quashed. The court listed it for 22 October, and no report of that hearing or of a later order was found
  • Further reading and viewing: Rajeev Kumar in The Wire on who controls ECINet, the Commission's software, during the revision

entry.content:

The bulk Form 7 table now marks Mustafabad as a police case

The Chief Electoral Officer, Naveen Mahajan, said the State Election Commission relied on the roll from before the revision
  • Protests and disputes: Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer said on 7 November, in reply to The Hindu's report on Mahadevapura, that more than one EPIC number was generated for one person where an applicant filed more than one Form 6 through the Citizen Service Portal, and that the cases have been sent for verification

  • Notices: Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer put the electors found ineligible after a notice at 54,418 on 6 November, Siasat reports

  • What to do now: the pages of the seven states now give the steps for an elector left off as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate from the Commission's letter of 6 November itself

entry.title: 7 November 2026: 3 additions
entry.summary: How the revision ran: the Commission wrote on 6 November to the Chief Electoral Officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland that electors left off the draft roll because they were marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate are to get one more opportunity
entry.content:
• How the revision ran: the Commission wrote on 6 November to the Chief Electoral Officers of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland that electors left off the draft roll because they were marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate are to get one more opportunity to be included in the final roll, by submitting the enumeration form with a statement, as Business Standard, PTI and The Wire report. An elector who moved within the state need not file Form 8, and a form accepted keeps the elector's earlier EPIC number
  • What to do now: the pages of the seven states give the steps for an elector left off the draft as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, from the Commission's letter of 6 November
  • Notices: the office of Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer said 32,35,212 of the electors sent the 33.1 lakh notices in Delhi had been parked for the final roll by 4 November, PTI reports

entry.title: Week ending 6 November 2026
entry.summary: On 3 November the Election Commission wrote to every Chief Electoral Officer that an elector left off the draft roll may file Form 6, and that no registration officer is to start action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 only because the elector was on an earlier roll and
entry.content:
• How the revision was run. On 3 November the Election Commission wrote to every Chief Electoral Officer that an elector left off the draft roll may file Form 6, and that no registration officer is to start action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 only because the elector was on an earlier roll and filed Form 6.
  • Protests and disputes. The Commission has taken the SIR declaration out of the online Form 6 in the states where the revision is still running and put it on ECINet as a separate form, The Indian Express reports.
  • How the revision was run. On 4 November the Commission ordered a special summary revision of the roll in Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim, with the final rolls due on 21 January 2027, and West Bengal's special summary revision, put back on 28 October, now has its draft roll due on 23 November.
  • Protests and disputes. On 4 November the Supreme Court said electors left off Delhi's draft need not fear filing Form 6 while it hears the case, declined urgent orders and will hear the petitioners' application on 19 November.
  • Protests and disputes. On 4 November the Supreme Court issued notice to the Centre and the Commission on petitions against section 16 of the Act of 2023 on the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners, which bars civil and criminal proceedings against any of them, serving or former, and listed the petitions for 18 December.
  • Protests and disputes. On 5 November the Bombay High Court at Goa held that a voter who moves house files Form 8 and cannot be made to file Form 6, directed the registration officer of Santa Cruz to include a family of six in the roll within ten days and refused the Commission a stay.
  • How the revision was run. Jharkhand's Chief Electoral Officer gave 45,49,961 logical discrepancy cases and 14,04,033 no-mapping cases on 4 November, with 14,88,802 and 7,95,415 of them still pending.
  • Left off the roll? What to do. Every state and union territory with a schedule for the revision now has a What to do now page, 32 in all, with the steps open to an elector on the day it is read, and a card on the front page leads to each of them.

entry.title: 6 November 2026: 18 additions
entry.summary: What's new: the week ending 6 November in eight sentences, each linked to the page that carries the fact, at the top of this page. A new issue follows every Friday
entry.content:
• What's new: the week ending 6 November in eight sentences, each linked to the page that carries the fact, at the top of this page. A new issue follows every Friday
  • Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court issued notice to the Centre and the Commission on 4 November on petitions by the RJD Member of Parliament Manoj Jha and an advocate against section 16 of the Act of 2023, which bars civil and criminal proceedings against a serving or former Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner, and listed them for 18 December
  • Protests and disputes: the Bombay High Court at Goa on 5 November directed the registration officer of Santa Cruz to include a family of six in the roll within ten days. It held that a voter who moves house files Form 8 and cannot be made to file Form 6, and that a registration officer is bound to decide Form 8 while a revision is under way. It refused the Commission a stay, and Dainik Gomantak TV reports the Commission's advocate, Gaurish Agni, as saying the Commission is moving the Supreme Court
  • Protests and disputes: the INDIA bloc's protest in Bengaluru on 5 November adopted a five-point resolution asking the Karnataka government to hold the panchayat and local body elections on the rolls of 2025, and the Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar, announced a police investigation into the alleged misuse of Form 7. The state Cabinet discussed the rolls the same day and took no decision
  • Protests and disputes: Mumbai Police asked the Foreigners Regional Registration Office to verify the OCI status of a second actor detained at the Mumbai protest of 10 October, against whom an FIR was registered, The Indian Express reports
  • Protests and disputes: The Times of India puts the panchayat and urban local body rolls in Uttar Pradesh at 16.91 crore electors in all, against 13.46 crore on the Assembly rolls on 7 October, a difference of nearly 3.45 crore. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, told the paper that the Assembly rolls have four qualifying dates and the panchayat rolls one, and that the urban comparison is not exact
  • How the revision ran: Inside the Commission adds the work allocation order of 4 November, which puts the Director General of IT's files through a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, The Indian Express reports
  • Notices: Jharkhand's Chief Electoral Officer gave 45,49,961 logical discrepancy cases and 14,04,033 no-mapping cases on 4 November, with 14,88,802 and 7,95,415 of them still pending
  • Events: the BJP's march in Shivamogga on 5 November, and the Cockroach Janta Party's protest at Rajendra Maidan in Kochi on 7 November
  • Further reading and viewing: Frontline on how 73,39,235 names came to be left off Telangana's draft roll, and Praveen Chakravarty of the Congress setting the count of adults with Aadhaar against the rolls of 14 states
  • Further reading and viewing: a panel on Praveen Chakravarty's column and post of 6 November, which set UIDAI's count of adults with Aadhaar against the rolls of 14 states, beside the final rolls and the projection of adults on the All India page
  • What to do now in Goa: a step for an elector who moved house within the constituency, from the Bombay High Court at Goa's judgment of 5 November in one family's case. The court held that a registration officer is bound to decide Form 8 while a revision is under way, and cannot reject it because Form 6 should have been filed
  • What to do now in Delhi: a step for an elector who finds a Form 7 filed against their name, or in their name, with the Commission's directive of 9 October on false Form 7 complaints as The Hindu quotes it, and the North East Delhi District Election Officer's statement that every Form 7 in Mustafabad would be checked in the field before a name is deleted
  • Tripura: the overview and its What to do now page give the schedule of 29 October, with house visits from 26 December, the draft roll due on 1 February 2027 and the final roll on 7 April 2027
  • What to do now: the notices table dates the no-mapping and discrepancy lists when they come from a later report than the count of notices, as Jharkhand's of 4 November do
  • Left off the roll? What to do: the step on Form 8 now gives the Bombay High Court at Goa's judgment of 5 November, which held that a registration officer who receives Form 8 is bound to decide it while a revision is under way, and that a family who moved house within their constituency and filed Form 8 could not be made to file Form 6
  • How the revision ran: a link to a state's dates from its own page now opens on that state's row in the schedule charts, outlined, with its dates written under the chart. The district pages of Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Mizoram, and the district and constituency pages of Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya and Odisha, no longer offer a map their state's page does not draw. Gujarat's constituency pages say that its map shows the district, a constituency that is the only one in its district no longer ranks 1 of 1 there, and Odisha's reserved constituencies are marked (ST) and (SC)
  • Questions and answers: the answer on where to find the names added and deleted after the draft, constituency by constituency, now names Bihar as well as Uttarakhand, and each of Bihar's 243 constituency pages shows them. The corrections page sets out what the answer said before

entry.title: 5 November 2026: 8 additions

entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: The Indian Express reports that a circular of 14 October set up the committee to check ECINet against the law, headed by a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner with four Chief Electoral Officers and experts from IIT Bombay and IISc Bengaluru, and that by the Commission's affidavit 88 of the 97 Goa electors left off the final roll have had their Form 6 applications accepted
  • Protests and disputes: The Hindu reports that 20 of the BJP's booth level agents are named as objectors in 787 of the 1,021 Form 7 applications filed in Delhi's Mustafabad, all of them against Muslim electors by the paper's account, and that 16 of the 20 denied filing or signing them. The bulk Form 7 table now gives 787 for Mustafabad
  • Protests and disputes: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, the petitioners in the Supreme Court case on Delhi's revision, wrote to the Commission and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer on 5 November asking for FIRs, an audit of every Form 7 filed in Delhi, a stay on deletions from third-party Form 7s until they are verified, and publication of every Form 7
  • How the revision ran: Inside the Commission adds the circular of 14 October that set up the committee to check ECINet
  • How the revision ran: the Commission ordered on 4 November a special summary revision of the roll in Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha and Sikkim, with the draft rolls due on 30 November, claims and objections until 30 December and the final rolls on 21 January 2027, The Indian Express and NewsDrum report. The claims box on each of the six states' pages gives these dates
  • Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer directed on 4 November that every Assembly constituency's roll be matched with the rolls of panchayats and urban local bodies, and that people registered at fair price shops be checked against it, to find eligible people missing from the roll, The Hindu and Aaj Tak report
  • Protests and disputes: the INDIA bloc in Karnataka protested at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on 5 November, demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, and said rallies would follow in every district
  • Events: the INDIA bloc protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru and Amit Shah's march in Karnal on 5 November
