  • Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court sought replies from Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi and the Centre on a plea by advocates over the march of 12 October to the Court, and listed it for 23 November
  • Protests and disputes: the Commission has taken the SIR declaration out of the online Form 6 in the states where the revision is still running and put it on ECINet as a separate form, The Indian Express reports
  • Protests and disputes: booth level officers in Delhi say they are being sent back to electors who gave only Aadhaar to collect more documents, and officials deny issuing any such instruction, The Hindu reports
  • Protests and disputes: The Hindu found 803 EPIC numbers linked to 397 people in Mahadevapura's final roll
  • Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer directed on 2 November that every rejected Form 6 application be re-examined
  • Protests and disputes: protesters staged a rail roko in Kanchipuram on 4 November demanding the arrest of the Chief Election Commissioner, and police detained them
  • Protests and disputes: the Kochi Corporation Council passed a resolution on 3 November in solidarity with the protests over the SIR, and the BJP councillors walked out
  • Protests and disputes: the Telangana Voter Rights Forum told a press conference on 3 November that its volunteers counted 43 electors wrongly left off in two polling stations of Secunderabad Cantonment and 42 of the 95 electors on the list they surveyed in Musheerabad, and asked that the revision be withdrawn
  • Events: the BJP's march in Giridih and the ABVP's march in Ranchi on 3 November, and the rail roko in Kanchipuram on 4 November
  • Help: the step on what the ordinary Form 6 asks you to sign now gives what the Commission's letter of 3 November says about electors who were on a roll before, and the What to do now pages give it to electors left off the draft and to those not on the final roll
  • Further reading and viewing: Frontline on the Sabar Institute's analysis of the names left off Telangana's draft roll in the 104 seats outside Hyderabad, where by Sabar's count about 50.2 per cent of the names are women's and more women than men were left off in 91 of the 104 seats

entry.title: 3 November 2026: 14 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer's office asked the judges of the appellate tribunals in late October to set up digital signature certificates through a private agency, with their PAN and identity cards and a video verification, after they stopped logging in to the Commis
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer's office asked the judges of the appellate tribunals in late October to set up digital signature certificates through a private agency, with their PAN and identity cards and a video verification, after they stopped logging in to the Commission's portal over its Aadhaar screen, The Indian Express reports
  • Protests and disputes: the Commission's Notice and Hearing Report of 22 February shows West Bengal's registration officers had left 8,88,889 hearing cases undecided at the deadline, while 60,06,675 electors were placed under adjudication a week later, The Wire reports
  • Protests and disputes: in Hyderabad, electors who had applied on Form 8 to change their address and did not return enumeration forms were left off the draft, and their Form 8 applications are now being rejected, The Hindu reports
  • Protests and disputes: officials in Telangana put the rejection of 1,92,574 Form 6 applications made before the revision down to the missing declaration form, The Hindu reports
  • Protests and disputes: Telangana's Chief Electoral Officer's figures show 50,908 Form 7 applications filed from 8 to 31 October, after claims closed, and 48,623 accepted. Officials told Telangana Today that a glitch in generating the data had brought earlier applications into the figures
  • Protests and disputes: the Bombay High Court kept in abeyance until 7 December the Leave India Notice issued to an actor holding an Overseas Citizen of India card, who was detained at a protest in Mumbai on 10 October against the Chief Election Commissioner over the SIR. He filed an unconditional apology and an undertaking not to take part in protests
  • Protests and disputes: Delhi Police registered an FIR against 22 people detained at Minto Road on 1 November as they marched from the INDIA bloc rally towards Jantar Mantar
  • Events: Amit Shah's foot march with the Telangana BJP in Hyderabad on 2 November, the march from the INDIA bloc rally towards Jantar Mantar on 1 November, and Sambit Patra's press conference on the SIR in Varanasi on 2 November
  • Front page: six lines on what the counts show, each linked to the page that carries its figure. Four stay the same: the share entered as dead among the names left off with a published reason, how much larger the final rolls were than the drafts, the notices sent, and the states where women were a larger share of the names left off. Two more change each day, from Bihar's lists, the large cities and the winning margins
  • Women: Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Manipur and Meghalaya join the states and union territories with the names left off by sex, which makes 15. In 10 of them women were a larger share of the names left off than of the roll
  • Women: third-gender electors on the roll before the revision and left off the draft, per 100, beside the rate for all electors, in 11 states and union territories
  • The SIR in brief: the section on the rights of anyone who protests now has the Supreme Court's order of 2 November in Aruna Roy v Union of India, which set aside the Rajasthan State Election Commission's refusal of voter awareness campaigns before the panchayat elections
  • All India: the All India page and the reading-page panels now describe the final-roll figure as the net change after the draft, the names added less the names deleted. The All India report is brought up to date, with the 15 states and union territories that published the names left off by sex, or their roll by sex before the revision and at the draft, and a table of third-gender electors
  • Further reading and viewing: PTI sets out the rolls of Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Manipur and Goa before the revision, at the draft and at the final roll, and puts the fall across the five at about 2.29 crore, or 12.2 per cent, with Uttar Pradesh at 13.24 per cent

entry.title: 2 November 2026: 7 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: the Election Commission ordered on 31 October that two Electoral Registration Officers of Pilibhit be suspended, that their chargesheets come to it for vetting, and that Section 198 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita be added to the FIR against them and a computer operator
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: the Election Commission ordered on 31 October that two Electoral Registration Officers of Pilibhit be suspended, that their chargesheets come to it for vetting, and that Section 198 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita be added to the FIR against them and a computer operator
  • Protests and disputes: in Hemtabad, Uttar Dinajpur, the Commission appealed against 15,381 of the 34,327 electors the judges had cleared, and 599 of the appeals carry the code for 5 April although the list that cleared those electors was published on 6 April, The Wire reports
  • Protests and disputes: The Hindu found errors in at least 1,000 entries of Bengaluru's final rolls, from garbled names in runs of serial numbers in Dasarahalli to relatives' names given as 'Husband Husband' or a single letter
  • Protests and disputes: Mohammed Zubair of Alt News posted on X that an elector in Mahadevapura who filed Form 6 twice now has five EPIC numbers. No news outlet has reported it and no official has answered it
  • How the revision ran: the Commission moved West Bengal's special summary revision on 28 October, at the Chief Electoral Officer's request, PTI reports. The draft roll is now due on 23 November, claims and objections run to 22 December and the final roll is due on 16 January 2027
  • Events: the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November as the reports give it, who spoke, who stayed away and how large the reports put the crowd, and the BJP's march in Delhi the same day
  • Further reading and viewing: the Sabar Institute's report on the 1,08,24,651 names left off Karnataka's draft roll, by reason, district, age, sex and constituency

entry.title: 1 November 2026: 7 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer ordered on 31 October that the ECINET login IDs of all computer assistants in registration officers' offices be disabled, after the misuse of those IDs in Pilibhit, and directed that the Pilibhit operator's services be ended
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer ordered on 31 October that the ECINET login IDs of all computer assistants in registration officers' offices be disabled, after the misuse of those IDs in Pilibhit, and directed that the Pilibhit operator's services be ended
  • Events: the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November now carries the name Rahul Gandhi gave it, the Vote Bachao Desh Bachao Jan March and Maharally, and the march's route from the Connaught Place and Minto Road junction by Ajmeri Gate
  • Protests and disputes: after The Hindu found at their addresses 28 electors in Delhi's Mustafabad against whom a BJP booth level agent, as the Commission's records name him, had filed Form 7 objections, the North East Delhi District Election Officer's office said on 31 October that officers would visit every elector named in a Form 7 there before deleting any name. The Hindu counts 684 of the constituency's 961 objections as filed by the BJP's agents
  • How the revision ran: the table of bulk Form 7 filings now has a row for Mustafabad in North East Delhi
  • Protests and disputes: volunteers of the Telangana Voter Rights Forum checked 174 of 721 electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate and found 40 of them living at the same addresses, The Hindu reports from the forum's public hearing for two polling stations in Secunderabad Cantonment
  • Events: the INDIA bloc's public impeachment of the Chief Election Commissioner on 31 October as it was held, the march to the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November, the BJP's marches in Rohtak, Faridabad and Shimla and the AAP's march in Rohtak on the same day
  • Further reading and viewing: the Internet Freedom Foundation on the 96 ArcGIS licences the Registrar General bought for Census 2027 under a Proprietary Article Certificate, at ₹14,38,74,322, and on ReliaQuest's report that a group it assessed with moderate confidence to be the China-backed Flax Typhoon kept a backdoor in an ArcGIS Server for over a year

entry.title: 31 October 2026: 19 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: The New Indian Express reports that the Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, Rajiv Ranjan Singh, said at a workshop in New Delhi on 30 October that a new panchayat scheme will make Aadhaar-based payments outdated, and that biometric authentication with the EPIC number will be the
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: The New Indian Express reports that the Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, Rajiv Ranjan Singh, said at a workshop in New Delhi on 30 October that a new panchayat scheme will make Aadhaar-based payments outdated, and that biometric authentication with the EPIC number will be the only valid way to receive payments and benefits. The ministry's release on the workshop does not mention EPIC, Aadhaar or biometric authentication
  • Protests and disputes: The Wire describes a screen recording of the Commission's officer portal in which a Deganga elector in North 24 Parganas was flagged for a logical discrepancy because six other electors had named the same man as their father, and the only option on the screen was a hearing
  • Protests and disputes: in the same report a leader of a booth level officers' association in West Bengal says the BLO app changed about 16 times during the revision and that the then Chief Electoral Officer told the association decisions were being taken in Delhi. The Wire has asked the former Chief Electoral Officer to confirm the remark
  • Protests and disputes: The Reporters' Collective compared 55 of Pilibhit's booths with the final roll of 10 April and found 2,691 entries whose names had been replaced after the revision, 2,638 of them still on the roll eight days after the Chief Electoral Officer's finding of 22 October
  • Protests and disputes: the same report says the Commission's manual and software let a registration officer start and approve a Form 8 correction without the booth level officer's field verification or any document uploaded, and that the correction forms the Commission discloses carry no EPIC number
  • Further reading and viewing: The Reporters' Collective on Pilibhit's roll and on the Form 8 rules and software it says apply in every state
  • Corrections: Jharkhand's claims and objections closed on 31 October and are to be decided by 23 November. The box on its pages had given 23 November as the last day for claims
  • How the revision ran: the Election Commission put back Tripura's revision a second time on 29 October, at the Chief Electoral Officer's request, because elections to urban local bodies are due. Booth officers now visit homes from 26 December to 25 January, the draft roll is due on 1 February 2027 and the final roll on 7 April 2027
  • Notices: Delhi, where about 32 lakh of the more than 33 lakh notices had been resolved by 30 October
  • Protests and disputes: booth level officers in Delhi are to record, in a new column of their app, why each elector left off the draft was marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate
  • Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer said District Election Officers will answer for errors and pending forms in their districts, and asked Pilibhit's present and former District Election Officers to explain the 10,470 erroneous forms accepted on Pilibhit Sadar's roll
  • Events: a Tripura BJP rally in Agartala backing the revision on 31 October, an ABVP march in Patna and a mock parliament in New Delhi on 30 October, and the Delhi Traffic Police's restrictions for the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November
  • Further reading and viewing: The Hindu on how few of the names left off Karnataka's draft came back, and on whether the officials who appealed against 16.10 lakh West Bengal electors had the power to
  • What to do now: a page for each of the seven states still in the revision, Delhi, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Haryana and Nagaland, with the steps open to an elector on the day it is read, from checking the draft roll and the forms to the notices, the hearings and the appeals, each with the order or law it rests on
  • What to do now: a card on the front page and an entry in the Start here menu lead to the page for each state
  • Left off the roll? What to do: Part III Action Research & Resource Centre in Delhi, which says it helped survivors of domestic violence apply in the revision and has published a guidebook in English and Hindi on each step of Delhi's revision, from the enumeration form to the appeals
  • Further reading and viewing: Part III's guidebook on the revision in Delhi, with Delhi's dates as revised on 29 October and the forms, documents, hearings and appeals
  • What to do now: every state and union territory with a schedule for the revision now has a page saying what an elector there can do at the stage the revision has reached, 32 in all where there were 7. Where the Commission has ordered a special summary revision, the page gives its dates, and West Bengal's gives the Supreme Court's orders on appeals to the tribunals
  • Left off the roll? What to do: section 23(3) of the 1950 Act is now given in its own terms, and the list of people entitled to free legal help is now the whole of section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act

entry.title: Week ending 30 October 2026
entry.summary: On 29 October the Election Commission moved the final rolls to 30 November in Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Nagaland and to 22 December in Delhi, at the request of the Chief Electoral Officers.
entry.content:
• How the revision was run. On 29 October the Election Commission moved the final rolls to 30 November in Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Nagaland and to 22 December in Delhi, at the request of the Chief Electoral Officers.
  • Protests and disputes. In an affidavit of 26 October the Election Commission told the Supreme Court that all three SIR orders were unanimous and that Form 6 was not amended, while accepting that the declaration shown online with it could be read as an amendment, and on 27 October the Court gave the petitioners 10 days to answer it.
  • Protests and disputes. At the Delhi hearing of 28 October the Supreme Court said orally that electors left off the draft who were on the 2026 roll should be allowed the enumeration form or Form 8 in place of Form 6, which is for first-time voters, and told the Commission to keep taking Form 6 and Form 8 with no 30 October cut-off, and no written order was reported.
  • Protests and disputes. On 30 October the Supreme Court told the Commission to examine the bulk Form 7 applications in Uttar Pradesh that the petitioners say remain unresolved and to file a compliance report, and it declined to extend the time for Kerala's revision.
  • Reserved seats, final rolls and borders. Meghalaya's final roll of 26 October holds 21,83,963 electors, a fall in the roll of 1,65,682 since the roll before the revision, and Karnataka's final roll of 27 October holds 4,54,55,689 general electors, a fall in the roll of 99,76,625 since the roll of 16 June.
  • How the revision was run. Telangana had held 92,08,443 hearings on notices by 29 October and found 50,690 electors ineligible, and Delhi had disposed of 31.2 lakh of its 33.1 lakh notices by 26 October.
  • Left off the roll? What to do. On the help page and on every state's page a box now shows whether claims and objections are open in that state today and when the final roll is due, and How the revision was run now lists the bulk Form 7 filings reported in each state.
  • Events. The INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of the Chief Election Commissioner was put back to 31 October because of rain, and BJP marches run in Rajasthan from 30 October to 5 November and in six Uttar Pradesh regions from 3 to 5 November.

entry.title: 30 October 2026: 17 additions
entry.summary: What's new: the week ending 30 October in eight sentences, each linked to the page that carries the fact, at the top of this page. A new issue follows every Friday
entry.content:
• What's new: the week ending 30 October in eight sentences, each linked to the page that carries the fact, at the top of this page. A new issue follows every Friday
  • Corrections: the Supreme Court's Delhi hearing of 28 October now gives both halves of what the bench said about the forms. It said electors on the 2026 roll who were left off the draft should be allowed the enumeration form or Form 8 in place of Form 6, which is for first-time voters, and it asked the Commission to keep taking Form 6 and Form 8 with no cut-off

In Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand the house-to-house count runs from 1 December 2026 to 4 January 2027, the day the summary revision's final rolls are due, and the other states and union territories, with Manipur, Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir left out, are counted from 25 January to 28 February 2027
  • How the revision ran: the Election Commission moved the final rolls on 29 October, to 30 November in Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Nagaland and to 22 December in Delhi, at the request of the Chief Electoral Officers. Claims now run to 13 November in Maharashtra and to 25 November in Delhi
  • Left off the roll? What to do: a box on the help page and on every state's page now says whether claims and objections are open in that state today and until when, when notices will be decided, and when the final roll is due
  • Protests and disputes: the hearings and deadlines ahead in the SIR cases, soonest first, from the Supreme Court's Maharashtra hearing on 5 November to the Bombay High Court's on 1 December, each with the report that gives its date. They are in the calendars too
  • Protests and disputes: on 30 October the Supreme Court told the Election Commission to examine the bulk Form 7 applications in Uttar Pradesh that the petitioners say remain unresolved, take corrective steps and file a compliance report
  • Protests and disputes: on 30 October the Supreme Court declined to extend the time for Kerala's revision and asked the petitioners to bring the electors who should still get a chance to the Commission's notice
  • Protests and disputes: The Wire on Murshidabad and Nadia, where the registration officers had decided almost every hearing by 21 February and far more electors were later sent to judicial officers, and the Commission's special roll observer for West Bengal on the 16 lakh appeals
  • Protests and disputes: in Telangana 4,54,340 electors were deleted on Form 7 between 1 January and 14 June, before the revision began, The Hindu reports from the Chief Electoral Officer's figures
  • Notices: Telangana's hearings stood at 92,08,443 on 29 October, with 50,690 electors found ineligible, and Andhra Pradesh's at 44,28,858, with 1,73,662 found ineligible
  • Events: the INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of the Chief Election Commissioner was put back to 31 October because of rain. BJP marches in Rajasthan from 30 October to 5 November, in Indore on 30 October and in six Uttar Pradesh regions from 3 to 5 November
  • Further reading: Veena Naregal in Scroll on what the revision takes from a decade of exclusion in welfare schemes, and The Hindu's editorial 'Deemed ineligible'
  • How the revision ran: every state's final roll date now has its own history, each revision in order with its source, the dates reported only in the press marked as such, and the number of times the date moved and the days it added. Delhi's moved from 7 October to 4 December and then to 22 December, and Telangana's from 1 October to 9 November and then to 30 November
  • How the revision ran: the hearings on notices, state by state, with each state's latest count of hearings held and of names deleted after a notice, each dated and linked to its source, and a chart of how the counts moved in Telangana, Delhi, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya
  • Reserved seats, final rolls and borders: every final roll beside its draft, with the roll before the revision, the names added and deleted after the draft and how far the figures add up, and the states still waiting for a final roll with the date each is now due
  • How the revision ran: bulk Form 7 filings reported, state by state, with the count each report gives, who filed them by role or party, what happened to them and links to the reports, beside the Commission's own limits on Form 7

entry.title: 29 October 2026: 6 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: at the Delhi hearing of 28 October the Supreme Court told the Election Commission orally not to hold electors to the 30 October cut-off, to keep taking Form 6 and Form 8 and to issue a public notice, without passing a written order. The matter returns in two weeks
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: at the Delhi hearing of 28 October the Supreme Court told the Election Commission orally not to hold electors to the 30 October cut-off, to keep taking Form 6 and Form 8 and to issue a public notice, without passing a written order. The matter returns in two weeks
  • Protests and disputes: in Sujapur and Samserganj the Commission has appealed against about half the electors the judges had cleared, and 72,838 of the 76,156 pending appeals carry one timestamp of 5 April, The Wire reports
  • Protests and disputes: a Karnataka coalition, SIR-Virodhi Karnataka, asks the State government to reject the final roll and to hold a social audit and public hearings
  • RTI: the Election Commission did not answer within 30 days an application of 25 September for the two Election Commissioners' recorded objections and the file notings on them
  • Events: the INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of the Chief Election Commissioner on 30 October has moved to 10 Rajaji Marg at 3:30 pm. BJP marches in Chandni Chowk on 28 October and in four Himachal Pradesh towns from 30 October to 4 November, a gathering in Thrissur on 30 October, and twelve more gatherings of 24 and 25 October from the People Against SIR map
  • Further reading and viewing: seven new items, among them the Hindustan Times on the about 1,600 suspected foreign nationals that officials in six states reported, Human Rights Watch on its 70 interviews, Jean Drèze and Yogendra Yadav on Uttar Pradesh's adults and final roll, two readings of the Commission's affidavit in The Wire, The Hindu's lead article on the May verdict, and The News Minute on Karnataka's final roll

entry.title: 28 October 2026: 9 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court asked the Election Commission on 28 October why Delhi electors left off the draft must apply on Form 6 as first-time voters when they were on the 2026 roll, and Justice Bagchi said the Court has not finally decided whether the logical discrepancy exercise is
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court asked the Election Commission on 28 October why Delhi electors left off the draft must apply on Form 6 as first-time voters when they were on the 2026 roll, and Justice Bagchi said the Court has not finally decided whether the logical discrepancy exercise is lawful. The Commission said it would examine the concerns and consider extending the 30 October deadline
  • Protests and disputes: the West Bengal appellate tribunals have asked the Election Commission at least twice since 24 September to remove an Aadhaar authentication step from its portal, without which they cannot upload final orders, as The Indian Express reported from official records

The fall in the roll is now 99,76,625, and the 10.08 lakh names added and 1.88 lakh deleted during claims and objections are now shown
  • Further reading and viewing: The Indian Express's editorial on the questions the Commission's affidavit leaves open, from the two Commissioners' objections to Goa's 97 voters and the West Bengal appeals
  • Further reading and viewing: Nishtha Gupta in The Hindu on how software matching replaced the presumption that a name on the roll is there lawfully, and what an error costs a voter
  • Further reading and viewing: The Hindu on the Congress's answer to the Commission's affidavit, which Jairam Ramesh called deceptive, deceitful and duplicitous, and Pawan Khera's post alleging that the government had posts about the affidavit taken down from Instagram, set beside LiveLaw's report that Instagram restricted and then restored its reel on the affidavit
  • Telangana: the figures for the draft now cite the Chief Electoral Officer's own post of 27 October 2026, which gives the same 73,39,235 names left off, 57,46,803 of them absent or shifted, 9,22,229 dead and 6,70,203 duplicate

entry.title: 27 October 2026: 13 additions
entry.summary: Meghalaya: the final roll, published on 26 October 2026, has 21,83,963 electors, a fall in the roll of 1,65,682 since the roll before the revision. entry.content:
• Meghalaya: the final roll, published on 26 October 2026, has 21,83,963 electors, a fall in the roll of 1,65,682 since the roll before the revision. It stands 14,720 above the draft and holds 10,59,743 men, 11,24,216 women and 4 third gender electors. After the draft 23,970 were added and 9,250 deleted, 6,724 of them after notice and hearing. The Chief Electoral Officer gave the final roll for the state only, with no table by district or constituency
  • How the revision was run: Meghalaya's final roll is marked as published on the state's calendar of dates
  • Karnataka: the final roll of 27 October 2026, 4,55,00,011 electors, a fall in the roll of 99,32,303 since the roll of 16 June. It stands 8,64,036 above the draft and holds 2,25,40,493 men, 2,29,12,355 women and 2,841 third gender electors. No count of names added or deleted after the draft was published, and no table by district
  • How the revision was run: Karnataka's final roll is marked as published on the state's calendar of dates
  • Protests and disputes: the Election Commission's affidavit in the Supreme Court, which says all three SIR orders were unanimous, that a suggestion or query by one Commissioner on a file is not a decision of the Commission, and that Form 6 was not amended although the declaration shown online with it could be read as an amendment. The Commission's press note of 26 September had said the declaration attached to Form 6 for the SIR was upheld by the Supreme Court
  • Protests and disputes: the Commission told the Supreme Court that the West Bengal appeals against the inclusion of electors were filed by officers of the state Chief Electoral Officer and were not placed before the Commission
  • Protests and disputes: The Indian Express's report of the same affidavit, which by the paper's account accepts that steps taken by officers on the online Form 6 needed to be corrected, sets out a review of ECINet by a committee with experts from IIT Mumbai and IISc Bengaluru, says 88 of the 97 Goa electors left off the final roll have since applied through Form 6, and says an order redistributing work among the Commission's officers in July was never implemented after the two Commissioners' joint direction
  • Further reading and viewing: The Indian Express's analysis of the Commission's affidavit, set against the notes of the two Election Commissioners its investigation reported
  • How the revision was run: the affidavit added to Inside the Commission as the Commission's reply, with what The Indian Express says it leaves unanswered
  • Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court adjourned the petitions on the Election Commission's functioning, the INDIA bloc's among them, and gave the petitioners 10 days to answer the Commission's affidavit. LiveLaw reported that the matter is tentatively listed on 17 November, and no interim order was reported
  • Protests and disputes: an FIR in Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh over Form 7 applications to delete 26 electors that were presented as signed by a man who cannot read or write, and the Congress, the Trinamool Congress and the Left asking West Bengal's State Election Commission to hold the Kolkata and Howrah civic polls only after deleted electors have been heard
  • Further reading and viewing: The Indian Express explains what the Commission's affidavit means for electors, and The Hindu sets the Commission's account of Form 6 against the Supreme Court's remark of 12 October
  • Further reading and viewing: The Hindu's visual story on India's first general election of 1951 and 1952, with how the first electoral rolls were prepared and published

entry.title: 26 October 2026: 15 additions

The Chief Justice orally assured that no elector deleted in the revision would
